summary.headline: H2 FY26 revenue rose 26% YoY to Rs 55.25 crore, with FY26 revenue at Rs 96.8 crore, up about 19.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 55.246 crore (+26% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 9.21 crore (+16.7% YoY, 16.61% margin) and PAT of Rs 5.19 crore (+20.73% YoY, 9.36% margin). For full FY26, revenue from operations was Rs 96.80 crore and total income Rs 98.34 crore, with EBITDA margin of 23.75% and PAT growth of 31.59%, as stated on the slide. Management said the third plant is commissioned, with plant reorganisation due in 3 to 4 weeks, and about 10 new machines added. Management guided to FY27 growth of roughly 20-25% or more, but declined to confirm the Rs 130 crore revenue and Rs 13 crore PAT figures raised by an analyst.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Ball valves are the largest product line, followed by butterfly valves, control valves and other valve types. Management said oil and gas is the largest end-use industry, with petrochemical, pharma, power, instrumentation and shipbuilding also served directly or indirectly.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Exports are about 26% of revenue and go to 14 countries, including Australia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK, USA and Brazil. Most export sales are on an ex-works basis.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected to grow about 20-25% or more, per management, with pipeline described as good.
EBITDA margin of about 17% (Q4 level) described as sustainable over the longer run.
Current capacity supports revenue of about Rs 140-150 crore annually without further capacity addition.
Management hopes to reach Rs 120-130 crore revenue in FY26 context; declined to commit to exact figures (Rs 130 crore revenue, Rs 13 crore PAT not confirmed).
FY27 capex planned at about Rs 2-3 crore for HMCs and inspection machines; 2-3 new machines already bought, still work in progress.
Dividend plans are still under consideration; no plans to raise equity currently.
capex_capacity: Third plant commissioned; plant reorganisation based on value stream mapping due to finish in 3 to 4 weeks to improve efficiency and utilisation.
About 10 new machines added, including special purpose machines, CNCs, HMCs, VMCs and multitasking machines; 5 already reported earlier.
Operating three shifts in the machining section; management sees scope for higher volumes via efficiency gains without new investment.
Third plant still has about 30-35% space, so brownfield expansion is possible.
Capacity ceiling stated at about Rs 140-150 crore annual revenue with existing setup.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose sharply after the Middle East conflict; management said increases are passed to customers, but higher material costs are slowing order conversion.
Order book about 20-22% of last year's revenue, mostly fulfilled within 6 to 10 weeks.
H2 revenue growth attributed to 2 to 3 large orders and some US tariff relaxations that allowed faster order conversion.
German customer: yearly business of about 1 million (currency unspecified) promised; open orders of more than 0.3-0.4 million since February; a second German customer pilot batch due in 4-6 months.
Middle East shipments slowed in March due to logistics disruption; management expects a rebound as oil field reconstruction starts.
Top 5 to 7 customers contribute about 65% of revenue; no single customer above 15-20%.

Competition is mainly small machining suppliers with narrow product focus; management says no one competes at its scale given forging, heat treatment and machining in-house, sizes from 0.5 inch to 24 inch.
Rejection rate below the industry benchmark of 1,800 DPPM, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What top line and EBITDA margin should shareholders expect for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line expected to grow about 20-25% or more; Q4 EBITDA margin of about 17% seen as sustainable, given rising raw material prices and slower order conversion.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material price inflation handled and can margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material increases are negotiated and passed to customers as components manufacturing is priced on market rates; management said price rises are slowing order wins, with stability expected in a few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach Rs 130 crore revenue and Rs 13 crore PAT this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it hopes to but would not comment on exact numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and how much will it be?
qa_highlights.answer: 2-3 new machines already bought plus inspection machines and HMCs; about Rs 2-3 crore, still a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room for growth beyond the Rs 140 crore capacity ceiling?
qa_highlights.answer: Brownfield expansion possible in the third plant, which has 30-35% space left; no detailed FY28 plan yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the main business risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs, the war and export pickup delays (last few crore of orders held back), raw material price volatility and customers seeking cheaper suppliers.

risks_watch: Raw material price volatility after the Middle East conflict is slowing order conversion.
Capacity ceiling of about Rs 140-150 crore may constrain FY28 growth until new capacity or brownfield expansion is commissioned.
Export delays and logistics slowness, especially for Middle East shipments.
Management declined to name the largest customer; top 5-7 customers are about 65% of revenue.
Borrowing mix has shifted toward short-term debt for Plant 3, per management's partial answer; monitor debt structure.
Dividend policy still under consideration; no decision yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 growth and the margin outlook, but cautious on near-term order flow, citing raw material volatility, the Middle East disruption and tariffs. Several answers were vague or deferred (FY27 guidance specifics, FY28 growth, dividends, shipbuilding contribution).

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of roughly 20-25% or more, backed by a commissioned third plant, about 10 new machines, spare capacity (current setup supports Rs 140-150 crore revenue without further additions), and an order book of about 20-22% of last year's revenue, but no specific order values or dated capacity numbers were given and it declined to confirm analyst FY26/FY27 figures.
